title: Terminal workflow: discover, create and test a datasource, publish, query, propose, approve as a separate principal, unpublish
promise: An operator runs the whole publication workflow from the installed command-line clients. The proposal comes from the agent surface (the installed MCP proxy, as in the terminal journey) and a different principal approves it with the typed approval command. The server's state after every command matches the fixture.

steps.description: List the published services; the fixture's sites service is listed.
Create a PostGIS datasource for the fixture database.
Test the stored datasource; the connection is healthy.
Publish the client's lifecycle table as a new service and layer.
List the datasource's layers for the service; the published layer is enabled.
Query the sites layer with the fixture filter; the features equal the filtered fixture rows with exact ordinates.
Count the published lifecycle layer's features; the count is the number of fixture rows.
As the proposer principal, find honua_publish_service in the setup view and call it to publish the client's proposal table; the server records a proposal awaiting approval instead of publishing.
The proposer tries to approve its own proposal; the command fails with 403 and the proposal is still awaiting approval.
The separate approver principal approves the proposal with the typed approval command.
Read the proposal until its status is terminal (bounded deadline): it succeeded, was requested by the proposer and resolved by the approver.
Query the layer the approval published; the features equal the proposal fixture rows with exact ordinates.
Query the unpublished layer; the command fails with not found (404).

honua-sdk-js.proposal-resolved: honua admin operate getOperationProposal --profile approver (until terminal)
